A.biggest_strength: Exhaustive and fully interactive coverage of 14 diverse languages, accompanied by tailored runtime cards, memory architecture diagrams, and flawless technical accuracy.
A.biggest_weakness: Lacks a prefers-reduced-motion media query, and comparison tables require horizontal scrolling on narrow mobile screens.

B.biggest_strength: Dynamic visual expression reduction with flying argument and return-value chips, complemented by real bytecode listings and empirical recursion benchmark charts.
B.biggest_weakness: Only 6 languages are supported in the interactive simulator, paired with an awkward initial state (step 13/13 with stack hidden) and truncated, invalid GCC assembly.
factual_errors: In Scene 6 ('Below the source'), the x86-64 GCC 13 assembly listing strips the function prologue and callee-saved register restoration while retaining 'leave' and clobbering '%ebx'; executing this code would corrupt '%rsp' and violate the System V ABI.

In the comparison table, JavaScript is stated as passing parameters by 'a reference to the same object (call by sharing)', which is incorrect for primitive numbers such as the 3 and 4 passed in the example (which are passed by value).

In 'What the figure leaves out', the claim that 'C and Rust cannot catch a stack overflow' overlooks that C programs on POSIX systems can catch the stack overflow SIGSEGV using an alternate signal stack via sigaltstack.
